description.en: The aim of the experiment is to verify KVL in a resistive DC circuit by observing that the sum of the voltage drops is equal to the applied source voltage.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.
The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.

The CALCULATE button auto-fills the resistance values in the theoretical verification section. For verification, you have to theoretically calculate the voltages using the provided equations and verify them using the VERIFY button.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.
The RESET button refresh the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.

Set the values of R1, R2, and R3 by moving the resistance sliders. These resistance values will remain constant throughout the experiment to ensure accurate verification of Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law.  

Range: 1 kΩ to 5 kΩ

This section provides the required DC voltage to the circuit. The display shows the active voltage supplied to the circuit, and the slider can be used to set the desired voltage value. 

Rating:  15 V DC

Voltmeters are used to measure the voltage drop across each resistor in an electrical circuit. Record the voltage readings across each resistor at different supply voltages. 

Rating:  0 - 20 V DC
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections by dragging and dropping wires between the connection points.
This table records the measured voltage drops V1, V2, and V3 at different source voltages. These readings will be used later to verify the KVL.
This section displays the equations you can use to verify Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law.

This section allows you to verify the KVL using the measured readings and the provided equations. Compare the calculated and measured voltages to confirm that the algebraic sum of all voltages around the closed loop is zero.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical verification, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, simulation summary, apparatus used, recorded readings, user-calculated results and conclusion.
